0.headline: Hi-Tech Flow files IPO papers to raise fresh capital of Rs 300 crore; Wealth Company to sell shares
0.heading: Hi-Tech Flow files IPO papers to raise fresh capital of Rs 300 crore; Wealth Company to sell shares
0.intro: HI-Tech Flow IPO | Wealth Company Asset Management is the only public shareholder in the company, while the remainder 85.33 percent stake is owned by promoters
0.body:
New Delhi-based HSAW pipe manufacturer Hi-Tech Flow has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise Rs 300 crore through a fresh issue.

The initial public offering (IPO) will also include an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares worth Rs 100 crore by promoters Ajay Kumar Bansal and Vipul Bansal.

Madhu Lunawat-backed The Wealth Company Asset Management, through The Wealth Company Alternates Trust – India Inflection Opportunity Fund, will also exit Hi-Tech Flow by selling all its 2.02 crore equity shares, representing 14.67 percent of the company's pre-offer paid-up equity, through the OFS.

The Wealth Company Asset Management is the only public shareholder in the company, while the remaining 85.33 percent stake is held by the promoters.

Hi-Tech Flow may also consider raising up to Rs 60 crore through a pre-IPO placement. If the pre-IPO placement is undertaken, the amount raised will be reduced from the fresh issue component.

The company plans to use Rs 125.9 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds to set up an API-grade HSAW pipe manufacturing unit, along with a 3LPE coating unit, at its existing Nagpur facility.

Another Rs 90 crore will be used to repay debt against outstanding borrowings of Rs 92 crore as of August 24, 2026. This would leave the company with minimal debt. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Hi-Tech Flow operates two manufacturing facilities in Sanand, Gujarat, and Nagpur, Maharashtra, with a total installed capacity of 1.6 lakh metric tonnes per annum (MTPA). The Sanand facility has a capacity of 40,000 MTPA, while the Nagpur facility has a capacity of 1.2 lakh MTPA.

The company is also undertaking an expansion of 30,000 MTPA at its Nagpur facility, which is expected to be completed by June 2027. This will take the facility's total annual capacity to 1.5 lakh MTPA.

The proposed expansion under the IPO's objects will add another 1.2 lakh MTPA, taking the overall capacity of the Nagpur facility to 2.7 lakh MTPA. The facility will also have an annual installed capacity of 10 lakh square metres for 3LPE coating of pipes, according to the DRHP.

On the financial front, Hi-Tech Flow, which competes with listed peers such as Ratnamani Metals &amp; Tubes, Man Industries, Welspun Corp and Jindal Saw, reported a 50.2 percent year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 36.4 crore for the year ended March 2026, from Rs 24.3 crore in the previous year.

Revenue during the period rose 40 percent to Rs 417.2 crore from Rs 298.3 crore a year earlier.

InCred Capital Financial Services and Pantomath Capital Advisors have been appointed as merchant bankers for the Hi-Tech Flow IPO.

1.headline: Elevate Campuses sees 2.5 million-bed student housing market, plans to scale ahead of IPO
1.heading: Elevate Campuses sees 2.5 million-bed student housing market, plans to scale ahead of IPO
1.intro: The Hillhouse-backed company, which is preparing to raise around Rs 2,100 crore through an IPO, plans to increase the contribution of student housing to 65-70 percent of its pro forma business from about 55 percent currently
1.body:
Elevate Campuses, India’s largest owner and manager of on-campus student accommodation, sees a 2.5 million-bed commercially viable market for organised student housing, giving it significant headroom to expand from its current portfolio of about 78,000 beds.

The opportunity comes as concerns over the safety and compliance of student accommodation have increased following accidents that have resulted in student deaths. Elevate believes its professionally managed, on-campus model could have an advantage over smaller and fragmented off-campus operators.

The Hillhouse-backed company, which is preparing to raise around Rs 2,100 crore through an IPO, plans to increase the contribution of student housing to 65-70 percent of its pro forma business from about 55 percent currently.

The company currently operates owned-and-managed and managed student accommodation assets, besides its K-12 schools business. On a pro forma consolidated basis, its revenue is around Rs 850 crore, including the K-12 business, which is currently housed in a different Hillhouse-managed fund and is being integrated into Elevate Campuses.

Elevate has partnered with major school operators, as well as large educational groups and institutions such as the Manipal University Jaipur and OP Jindal Global University, to own and operate student accommodation and allied facilities, including dining, healthcare and common-use areas.

The company estimates that India has roughly 12 million student accommodation beds, but only around 2.5 million are commercially viable for professionally managed accommodation. Elevate currently owns and manages around 78,000 beds, leaving it with a relatively small share of the addressable market.

“For every 200 enrolments in India, in graduate enrolments, we have less than one professionally managed student accommodation bed. It’s a big opportunity for us,” said Narasimha Jayakumar, CEO, Elevate Campuses.

On-campus model offers an edge

Elevate’s strategy is to focus on on-campus accommodation rather than the fragmented off-campus paying guest (PG) market. The company believes its presence on university campuses reduces occupancy risks and allows it to provide services such as security, access control, gyms, cafeterias and laundry.

The company also argues that its business model is less exposed to the seasonality typically associated with student accommodation. Fees for accommodation and services are collected in advance for the full academic year, rather than being dependent on monthly occupancy.

“The problem that you describe is faced by the off-campus players. We don’t face it because we are on campus,” said Vinod Rao, Chief Financial Officer of Elevate. “We collect the hostel fees and the fees for our services in advance for the full academic calendar.”

Elevate’s owned-and-managed model involves owning the land and building either on a freehold basis or through long-term leases, typically extending 50-60 years. Under its managed model, the university owns the asset while Elevate operates it for a management fee or revenue share.

The company estimates unlevered returns from student accommodation at around 9 percent, with escalation of 5-6 percent over the lease term, implying potential overall returns of around 15-16 percent, according to the management.

IPO to fund growth, reduce debt

The IPO is expected to raise around Rs 2,100 crore. Of this, about Rs 1,100 crore is earmarked as growth capital, while Rs 750 crore will be used for debt reduction.

The company has gross debt of around Rs 4,000 crore and net debt of about Rs 3,400 crore, with cash of around Rs 600 crore on its books.

The remaining Rs 250 crore will be used for general corporate purposes, including acquisitions.

Elevate believes the public-private partnership model could open another avenue for growth as more educational institutions look to outsource student accommodation.

The management pointed to potential opportunities with IITs and other institutions. The company has signed an agreement with IIT Madras to develop on-campus accommodation for doctoral candidates, while also identifying foreign universities setting up campuses in India as a potential customer segment.

“Twenty-one foreign universities are approved to set up campuses in India, and we also become a natural partner potentially for them,” Jayakumar said when asked about growth avenues for the company.

Positioning student housing as an asset class

Elevate is positioning student accommodation as an asset class that combines characteristics of commercial real estate assets such as REITs and hospitality. Unlike a conventional commercial property, however, the business has a significant operating component because of the range of services provided to students.

“We have REIT-like characteristics, but we’re a lot more than just a REIT,” Jayakumar said. “It’s also got a very strong operations layer akin to hospitality.”

The company said it generally takes over existing campus assets that have already received approvals relating to fire safety, occupancy and other regulatory requirements.

While greenfield projects can have a longer gestation period, the company said these account for a relatively small part of its business. For acquired or existing assets, revenue and EBITDA generation begins from the time the asset is acquired.

The company also intends to remain focused on India rather than expand overseas, citing the size of the domestic opportunity.

2.headline: Subscribe for ArMee Infotech Ltd IPO; Anand Rathi
2.heading: Subscribe for ArMee Infotech Ltd IPO; Anand Rathi
2.intro: Anand Rathi, has come out with its report on ArMee Infotech Ltd The research firm has recommended to “ Subscribe” the ipo in its research report as on September 18, 2026.
2.body:
Anand Rathi, ArMee Infotech Ltd
ArMee Infotech Limited is an IT infrastructure and IT managed services Company, which has ventured into the retail sales space through Experience Zones engaged in the sale of IT, consumer electronics, and gaming and merchandise products, and engaged in the Renewable Energy Space, including engineering, procurement and construction (“EPC”) of solar power projects and development of solar power projects under power purchase agreements (“PPAs”) and Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”). The company is headquartered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat and services both Government/public sector undertakings (PSUs) and private sector clients including wherein the end users are Government / PSUs which operate across a wide variety of industries. A majority of the company’s revenues are currently derived from servicing Government/PSU projects.

Valuation and Outlook
At the upper price band, the company is valued at 26.2x FY26 P/E and 17.83x FY26 EV/EBITDA, implying a post-issue market capitalization of ₹11,899 million. The company’s established presence in IT Infrastructure and IT Managed Services, sizeable Government/PSU client base, strong ongoing project pipeline and expansion into Renewable Energy provide multiple avenues for growth. Accordingly, we recommend a “Subscribe – Long Term” rating for the issue.
